provenance.platform: Windows 11, Intel i7-1355U (2 P-cores + 8 E-cores, 12 logical), CPU only, UNPINNED -- deliberately not the 8-core affinity the 2026-08-23 reading used; see the speed caveat below.
provenance.note: Re-read of the sealed holdout after two corrections landed. (1) The JATS projection stopped printing a space the page does not print (#470), so the GROUND TRUTH changed: 13 more table blocks are attainable (132 -> 145) and none stopped being. (2) all2md's outputs were regenerated at 2925f5c, which carries the row-grouping fixes #468 and #469 that the 2026-08-28 outputs (689ca1a) predate. The baselines were NOT re-run: docling and pymupdf4llm markdown is byte-identical to the 2026-08-28 reading, re-scored against the corrected truth. That is deliberate -- it holds the baseline side fixed so the movement is attributable. Every precision-side figure (novel share, raw precision, duplication, control) reproduced to every recorded digit across the re-scoring, because those instruments never touch JATS; that is the consistency check that licenses the recall movement.
provenance.table_gap_decomposition: The published 16.7-point table gap to docling is now 6.2. Of the 10.5 points closed, 7.1 are the truth correction and 4.1 are #468 + #469. The truth correction is not all2md gaining: on the 132 tables attainable under both truths NO tool's recovery changed at all (all2md 92, docling 114, pymupdf4llm 83, before and after). The whole of it is the 13 newly attainable tables, of which all2md recovers 8, pymupdf4llm 5 and docling 1. Those 13 are the tables dense in glued inline markup -- X1/X2, RRHF, 0.552a, NSCLCb, Willis43 -- which the old truth spelled with spaces the page does not print, putting them outside the ceiling for everyone. docling prints 'X 1' and '0.552 a' inside a table cell where the page prints 'X1' and '0.552a'; all2md reads the text layer literally.
provenance.speed_caveat: seconds_per_article_mean is NOT comparable to the 2026-08-23 reading and should not be quoted against it. All three tools measured 1.8-2.5x slower than their own records in this session. That is not a regression: all2md v1.13.0, built from its tag in a worktree, measured within 2% of HEAD on the same nine articles in the same session. Two unrelated third-party tools drifting the same direction points at ambient machine state -- the earlier reading ran overnight on an idle laptop, this one shared the box -- and a 15W U-series part throttles under sustained ONNX load. The RELATIVE ordering is robust and is what this column is good for: all2md remains the fastest of the three by 1.7x over pymupdf4llm and 3.0x over docling. Absolute values are a property of the machine that day. Note also that pinning to logical cores 0-7 on this hybrid CPU costs a further 2.3x on the ONNX layout path.
